gap: No cited result ChatGPT got lines up the UGREEN 1-monitor HDMI KVM and the TESmart HKS201-P23 on the same terms: both list the same video modes (4K@60 Hz, 2560×1440@120 Hz, 1920×1080@240 Hz). The only thing the TESmart's higher price buys that I could source is EDID emulation, so windows don't rearrange when you switch, plus hotkey, mouse-wheel and IR switching with a pass-through mode for gaming keyboards.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages. DeskDNA lists the UGREEN 1-monitor HDMI KVM at 4K60/1440p120/1080p240 with HDR and four USB 3.0 ports, and says nothing about EDID or hotkeys. It praises EDID emulation only on TESmart's DisplayPort 4K144 model and never mentions the HKS201-P23. iTechGuides already quotes UGREEN listings: 'EDID emulation is not supported' and 'Not support Keyboard shortcuts (hotkeys) toggles'. But those quotes are on its UGREEN 2-monitor model, and it doesn't cover the HKS201-P23. Neither page states chroma (4:4:4 vs 4:2:0) for any product. Neither notes that a DisplayPort KVM's 4K144 depends on DSC from the host. So the side-by-side 'same video modes, so the extra money buys EDID plus hotkeys' footnote is only half new.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's split but changes the reason. For a 4K60, 1440p120 or 1080p240 monitor, the UGREEN and the TESmart are equal on picture by their stated modes. Choose the HKS201-P23 only if windows jumping around on switch, or reaching for a button instead of a hotkey or mouse wheel, would bother you. Otherwise the cheaper UGREEN is enough. The StarTech DP 1.4 unit is only worth it for a monitor above 1440p120 or 4K60. I couldn't source the condition its 4K144 claim depends on, so the page should not promise 4K144 without checking the maker's spec.
